questions.question: How sharp is the main subject?

real_s1.explanation: The unit responds to vehicles (and some vehicle-like objects) seen in sharp focus, filling much of the frame, and especially when they face or point to the right, as in a side or three-quarter view. Its activity drops for blurry subjects, for head-on or rear views, for scenes with no single main subject, and for photos with a warm color tint. The preference for a rightward orientation over a frontal one, and for untinted photos, seems particular to this unit. The sharpness preference is partly shared with one similar unit.

real_s2.explanation: The unit responds to vehicles and vehicle-like machines (trucks, buses, cars, forklifts, plus parking meters and grilles) when the subject is sharply in focus, seen side-on and especially facing right rather than head-on, large in the frame and level, without a warm color cast. The strongest particular signals are sharpness versus slight blur and facing right versus toward or away from the camera. The similar units share neither.

real_s3.explanation: The unit responds to vehicles (cars, trucks, buses, and similar) shown in sharp, clear side or three-quarter views. It is most active when the subject faces or points to the right and is in focus, and somewhat more active on large, partly cut-off subjects with untinted color. It is less active on blurry subjects, on subjects seen head-on or from behind, on warm-tinted photos, and on scenes with no single main subject.

null_s1.explanation: The unit responds to vehicles (trucks, buses, cars) and similar boxy man-made objects. Within these classes it is most active on photos with a warm (yellow, orange or red) or neutral color cast and weaker on cool blue or green tinted photos. It also prefers a sharply focused main subject over a slightly blurry one. There is a weak hint that it prefers subjects placed in the left third of the frame, but only 5 photos support this.

null_s2.explanation: This unit responds to vehicle-dominated scenes such as trucks, buses, cabs and emergency vehicles. Within those classes, its clearest distinctive preference is for warm-tinted or neutral color over cool blue or green tints. It is also somewhat more active when the main subject is sharp rather than slightly blurry. Facing direction, subject size, cropping and tilt barely matter. The left-third position effect looks strong, but it rests on only 5 photos and is shared with a similar unit.

null_s3.explanation: A vehicle-oriented unit (pickups, wagons, forklifts, cabs, fire engines, buses) whose response depends little on composition, framing or facing direction. Its most distinctive variation is color tint. It is clearly weaker on photos with a cool blue or green tint and somewhat stronger on warm-tinted or neutral photos. It also prefers a sharp main subject over a slightly blurry one and medium lighting over bright, but the sharpness preference is partly shared with a similar unit. Being stronger when the subject sits in the left third is shared with similar units and rests on only 5 photos.
